clue.text: Supporter wanting much more tuned in around end of match

parts.note: well can mean much, as in well over the limit or well ahead

indicators.note: around says the second piece wraps round the letter that follows it

parts.note: wiser means more aware, better attuned to what is going on

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of the word match

explanation.surface: A fan, keen and more switched on than ever, as the final whistle approaches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting' is a link here. 'around' puts H (the last letter of 'match') inside WISER, giving WISHER after WELL.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who hopes another person does well is a supporter of theirs; the hyphenated noun names exactly that backer.

clue.text: Ladies holding one end of thick, light COME fibre

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Ladies holding one end of thick, light COME fibre' has a stray word COME the blank scan cannot resolve; wordplay WC round I + K is clear but the printed clue is unknown
annotationWithheld.clue: Ladies holding one end of thick, light COME fibre

clue.text: Bird in red gets drink for nothing

indicators.note: for says one piece is put in place of another: drink stands where nothing stood

parts.note: to be in the red is to be in debt, owing money
nothing is zero, the letter O
to lap is to drink as a cat does, with the tongue

explanation.surface: A bird dressed in scarlet is handed a free drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drink for nothing' looks like a free round, but it means swap LAP in for the O of OWING. 'in red' means in debt, not wearing red.
explanation.definitionFit: The peewit, a crested plover of farmland and moors, is a bird.

clue.text: Easing past women's crew in Olympic event

indicators.note: past says the easing piece comes after the women's crew in the answer

parts.note: W is the standard abbreviation for women
a rowing eight is a crew of eight oarsmen
lifting, as in lifting restrictions, means easing them

explanation.surface: A boat of women rowers being overtaken at the Olympics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'past' puts LIFTING after W and EIGHT. The rowing picture is a decoy: the event is not on the water at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising barbells in the snatch and the clean and jerk is a medal sport at the Games.

clue.text: Not facing the wrong one's done

indicators.note: wrong says these letters are set out incorrectly, to be rearranged

parts.note: one is I and the 's stands for is, giving I then S
taken as written

explanation.surface: A complaint that the mistake someone made has been finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges IS plus DONE. In cricket a batsman standing side-on has the shoulder, not the chest, towards the bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: A side-on stance turns the body sideways, so it is a posture not facing square to something.

clue.text: Peer over uninteresting brew

indicators.note: over places the peer above the next piece in this down entry

parts.note: an earl is a peer of the realm
grey means dull and uninteresting

explanation.surface: A nobleman bending over a boring pot of tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' is a down-clue charade sign: the first piece sits on top.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea flavoured with bergamot is a classic brew.

clue.text: Hands back in exchange

indicators.note: back says the word for hands is read from right to left

parts.note: paws is an informal word for hands

explanation.surface: Hands passed back as part of a trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns PAWS round.
explanation.definitionFit: To trade one thing for another is to exchange them, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Prime Minister gets stick after upsetting police

indicators.note: after says the stick comes behind the upturned piece
in a down clue, upsetting turns the word for police upside down, so it reads upwards

parts.note: the law is slang for the police
a pole is a long stick

explanation.surface: A Prime Minister faces a caning after a scandal that rocked the police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsetting' reverses LAW to WAL; 'after' puts POLE behind it. Robert Walpole is usually counted as Britain's first Prime Minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Robert Walpole led the British government from 1721 to 1742, the first holder of the role.

clue.text: Going after some romance with a correspondent?

definitions.meaning: putting a later date on a document, so following in time
courting a pen pal by letter, love through the mail

explanation.surface: Chasing a love affair with someone met through letters.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, the second definition is going on dates by post, a romance carried on through letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Dating a cheque later than today makes it come after the present, hence following.

clue.text: Put dice out, being ineligible for game

indicators.note: out says the letters are thrown out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A gambler throws the dice away and is barred from the match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges PUT DICE. A footballer is cup-tied when, having played in a cup for one club, he cannot play in it for another.
explanation.definitionFit: A cup-tied player is barred from a knockout competition, so is ineligible for that match.

clue.text: Draws oneself farther back, to an extent

indicators.note: back says the hidden letters are read backwards
to an extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Pulling oneself further backwards, at least partly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to an extent' finds SELFFAR inside 'oneself farther'; 'back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A lottery with prizes drawn from tickets is a draw; the plural noun matches.

clue.text: Future supplier will provide mint over the counter

parts.note: a mint is slang for a fortune, a huge sum of money
a bank teller serves customers over the counter

explanation.surface: A promise that someone will hand over freshly minted coins at the shop counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will provide' is a link. The mint and counter suggest a bank; the supplier of the future is a seer.
explanation.definitionFit: A clairvoyant who predicts what is to come supplies glimpses of the future.

clue.text: Shopkeeper makes quiet tick in index, maybe

indicators.note: in says the quiet and tick pieces go inside the finger

parts.note: the index is one example of a finger, hence maybe
sh is a call for quiet
a mo, a moment, is a tick, as in wait a tick

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper puts a quiet tick against an entry in the index.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts SH and MO inside FINGER. 'index' is not a list but the forefinger.
explanation.definitionFit: A seller of fish keeps a shop, so the trader is one kind of shopkeeper.

clue.text: Much-used ball left mark on snooker table

parts.note: a ball is round, like the letter O
the D is the semicircle marked at the baulk end of a snooker table

explanation.surface: A worn ball leaves a stain on the snooker table.
explanation.walkthrough: A snooker table has a D-shaped line at one end from which the cue ball is played.
explanation.definitionFit: Something worn by long service is old, as in an old coat that has seen much use.

clue.text: Exact image? One can do no more changes!

definitions.meaning: a perfect lookalike or double of someone

definitions.text: One can do no more changes!
definitions.meaning: a deceased bell-ringer can no longer ring changes, the sequences in change-ringing

explanation.surface: A perfect copy, and someone who can no longer alter anything.
explanation.walkthrough: In change-ringing, the bell-ringing art of English churches, a sequence of bell orders is a change.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who looks exactly like another is called this, a lookalike or spitting image.

clue.text: Early communist sponsors want new leader

indicators.note: want new leader says the sponsors' word needs a different first letter

parts.note: angels are backers, financial sponsors of theatrical shows

explanation.surface: Backers of an early communist want someone new in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'want new leader' swaps the first letter of ANGELS, A, for E. Friedrich Engels co-wrote The Communist Manifesto with Marx.
explanation.definitionFit: Friedrich Engels, Marx's collaborator in the 1840s, was one of the first communist thinkers.

clue.text: Superlatively fast remedies in place

indicators.note: in says the remedies go inside the word for place

parts.note: to set something is to place it
cures are remedies

explanation.surface: The quickest remedies are already in position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts CURES inside SET, between SE and T.
explanation.definitionFit: Fast can mean firmly fixed, so the most firmly fixed is the superlative of secure.

clue.text: Scorer confounded whingers

indicators.note: confounded means thrown into confusion, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A composer driven mad by complainers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confounded' rearranges WHINGERS. 'Scorer' is not a goalscorer but someone who writes musical scores.
explanation.definitionFit: George Gershwin wrote scores such as Rhapsody in Blue, so he is a composer.

clue.text: Wimp paid for supply in small instalments

parts.note: a drip is a feeble, wet person
fee'd, having paid a fee, read as feed

explanation.surface: A wimp is paid to deliver goods bit by bit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'paid for' is read as FEE'D, with a fee paid.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass something on a little at a time, as fluid through a tube, is to dole it out slowly.

clue.text: State one way to retain flair

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: to retain says the road abbreviation holds the flair inside it

parts.note: RD is the abbreviation for road, a way
elan is dash or flair

explanation.surface: Someone states a method for keeping their talent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to retain' puts ELAN inside RD, after I.
explanation.definitionFit: Ireland is an independent republic, a sovereign nation or state.

clue.text: Render senseless fine English in chapter's header

indicators.note: in says the fine and English pieces go inside the chapter's head

parts.note: a dean heads a cathedral chapter
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A fine for an Englishman, issued at the start of a chapter, leaves him stunned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts F and E inside DEAN. 'header' looks like a chapter heading; it is the clergyman at the head of the chapter.
explanation.definitionFit: Making someone unable to hear removes one of their senses.

clue.text: Dandy's captivating allure that shines amid the gloom

indicators.note: captivating means holding captive, so the dandy surrounds the allure

parts.note: a fop is a dandy, overly concerned with dress
glam, glamour, is allure

explanation.surface: A dandy whose charm glows in the darkness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'captivating' puts GLAM inside FOP; the 's is has, a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A car's fog light is designed to cut through mist, shining in gloomy conditions.

clue.text: Cook up and serve a little rum

indicators.note: up, in a down clue, says the word for cook reads upwards

parts.note: to do food is to cook it, as in done to a turn
to dish is to serve food

explanation.surface: Instructions to prepare and serve a small measure of spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses DO to OD before DISH. 'rum' looks like the drink but means strange.
explanation.definitionFit: Rum means odd, and the suffix ish softens it to somewhat strange.

clue.text: Carp when inspiration falls short

indicators.note: falls short says the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a bright idea is an inspiration

explanation.surface: Grumbling when creativity runs dry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'falls short' cuts the last letter from IDEA. 'Carp' looks like a verb (grumble) but is the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The ide is a freshwater fish of the carp family.

clue.text: Batsman's touch giving his team advantage

parts.note: a batsman's team is the side that is in, batting, read as IN SIDE
an edge is an advantage over rivals

explanation.surface: A lucky snick that gives the batting side the upper hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'his team' refers back to the batsman: his side is the one batting, the side that is in. 'giving' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A ball glancing off the inner side of the bat is a cricketer's deflection or snick.

clue.text: Buzzers used in spelling contests

definitions.meaning: competitions where children spell words aloud

explanation.surface: Buzzers sound in a spelling competition.
explanation.definitionFit: Insects that hum are buzzers, and a spelling competition is also called this.

clue.text: Short girl's good to travel with round city

indicators.note: round says the good, travel and with pieces go round the girl

parts.note: to go is to travel

indicators.note: short says the word for girl loses its last letter

parts.note: a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A petite girl's happy to travel round with a city break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' cuts LASS to LAS; 'round' puts G, GO and W round it, LAS going after G.
explanation.definitionFit: Glasgow is Scotland's largest city, on the River Clyde.

clue.text: Reform me: I fall into disrepute

indicators.note: reform means form again, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A plea to be changed for the better before a fall into disgrace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reform' rearranges ME I FALL; 'into' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A bad reputation, as in a house of ill fame, is disrepute.

clue.text: Swimmer stripped nude in middle of garden

indicators.note: in says the stripped piece goes inside the middle of the next word
middle of takes the central letters of garden
stripped says the word nude loses its outer letters

explanation.surface: Someone strips naked to swim in the middle of the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stripped' takes UD from NUDE; 'middle of' takes RD from GARDEN; 'in' puts UD inside RD. 'Swimmer' is a fish, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: The rudd is a freshwater fish, and fish are crossword swimmers.

clue.text: Near collapse, he's prone to turns

indicators.note: turns says these letters turn about into a new order

explanation.surface: A man inclined to fainting fits is about to keel over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' rearranges HE'S PRONE TO. A boxer on the ropes is close to defeat.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxer pinned against the ring ropes is close to being beaten, so near collapse.
